brief: Oil holds above $100/b (Brent near $101, WTI above $96) as Iran warns it will intensify attacks if US strikes continue, raising Strait of Hormuz disruption risk. Trump has signaled the conflict could run past the November midterms, and US officials reportedly weigh a much longer war, which the report says could keep a geopolitical premium in crude and refined-product prices. OPEC output fell 900kb/d to 19.9mb/d in August, reversing two months of recovery, as Saudi output dropped 1.1mb/d to 7mb/d, with exports down about a third, on tanker attacks through Hormuz and Houthi threats to the Red Sea route. Higher Iraqi and Venezuelan output only partially offset this, and Iraq is seeking a higher 6mb/d quota baseline. Gold holds near $4,400/oz. Higher Treasury yields, after a $6bn government debt purchase failed to lower borrowing costs, are a headwind, while Middle East-driven inflation concerns, a roughly 65% priced Fed hike probability, de-dollarisation and hedge demand provide support, with this week's PPI and CPI seen as decisive. Separately, PIF launched a privately co-financed Al Khafji coastal development, and GCC credit spreads traded modestly wider on risk-off flows and new-issue supply.
